NOTES.text:
Separate the stages of solving a computational problem. Analysis identifies the required result, inputs, constraints, and special cases. Design turns that understanding into an algorithm or data representation. Implementation expresses the design in a programming language.

Testing compares actual outputs with expected behavior on representative and boundary inputs. A syntax error means the program violates Python's grammar; a logic error means it runs but computes the wrong result. Passing one example is not proof of correctness, so use cases that challenge assumptions.

There may be several valid designs. Compare them against clarity, correctness, and resource requirements instead of treating the first working program as the only solution.
